capabilities.name: Real NISAR GUNW and GOFF products, read from HDF5
capabilities.evidence: 6 granules pass the QA gates; inspector values match the source arrays. On 13 Nov the rebuild added 5 Track 48 GUNW granules, and the second viewing direction added Pair B's GUNW (Track 98 frame 16) and 4 more Track 98 pairs, all through the same QA gates.

capabilities.name: GCOV backscatter snapshots for Rasuwa
capabilities.evidence: Not downloaded (about 31 GB). The Tsho Rolpa case does use GCOV.

capabilities.name: Line-of-sight displacement
capabilities.evidence: Deliberately absent: Pair A holds no usable phase at the source, and the sign convention is not yet confirmed. Tsho Rolpa movement bounds are research output only.

capabilities.name: Evidence class on every layer, panel and report
capabilities.evidence: Observed, Derived, Forecast, Hypothesis, Reference, Scenario, Unknown.

capabilities.name: Radar Observability: can the radar see a change, can it measure movement
capabilities.evidence: Method version 2, rebuilt from the raw files on 13 Nov: the product's own mask is applied (read as the 32-bit field it is), missing inputs are marked not assessed, and Rasuwa combines frames 74 and 75. The detachment zone has no valid data in the product (mask value 10: no valid subswath in the 28 Aug acquisition). Version 1 figures are withdrawn.

capabilities.name: Radar Observability for frame 75 (lower Rasuwa corridor)
capabilities.evidence: Frame 75 is assessed with its own event and pre-event pairs, where frame 74 does not reach. Frame 74 assesses 2,485,353 cells and frame 75 adds 1,584,616. 14% of the mapped mudflow and 18% of the Trishuli corridor lie outside both frames.

capabilities.name: Radar Observability from the opposite side (Track 98, ascending), beside Track 48
capabilities.evidence: Method version 2 on Track 98 frame 16 (event 19-31 Aug, before 26 Jul-19 Aug), as its own view, compared cell by cell with Track 48 and never merged. The inspector and report answer per direction from each one's own flags. Detachment zone: change judgeable on 35% from Track 98 (none from Track 48), movement on none from either.
tests: frontend/e2e/real.spec.ts::each viewing direction is judged on its own

capabilities.name: Before/after comparison against untouched ground
capabilities.evidence: 5 frame-74 pairs from prepare_control_series.py, with block-bootstrap 95% intervals: mudflow 0.38 to 0.19 against nearby ground 0.40 to 0.50, and across the event the intervals do not overlap; then the gap narrows. Consistent with surface change; it does not establish the cause, and the pre-event pair is longer and in a different radar mode. From the opposite side (Track 98), all five pairs in one radar mode: 0.31 against 0.40 before, 0.13 against 0.49 across the event.

capabilities.name: Change timeline at any clicked spot
capabilities.evidence: Coherence for five Track 48 pairs over frames 74 and 75 (23 Jul to 3 Oct 2026) and five Track 98 frame 16 pairs (26 Jul to 6 Oct), one layer each with a step per pair; the inspector chart shows a clicked spot pair by pair, one stored value per pair, and Time replay switches series. Rebuilding frame 74 with frame 75 reproduced all 360 frame 74 files byte for byte.

capabilities.name: "What could explain this?" for a clicked spot
capabilities.evidence: Rule-based, five explanations. Each viewing direction (Track 48 and Track 98) is read from its own flags and pair, and each check is labelled with its track. Only radar values at the spot and independent mapping count; without a radar value from any direction it says it cannot judge. Never a probability.
tests: frontend/e2e/real.spec.ts::explanations read Track 98 where Track 48 cannot see

capabilities.name: Evidence report: printable/PDF, CSV, GeoJSON, JSON
capabilities.evidence: Built in the browser from shipped data.

capabilities.name: Landslide-prone terrain (Model A, terrain only)
capabilities.evidence: A one-event consistency check, not a validation: 56% of the 2026 detachment zone screens High or Very high, against 32% of the whole area (AUC 0.66, with unmapped ground counted as negative).

capabilities.name: Road exposure along the Rasuwa corridor
capabilities.evidence: 250 m segments of trunk to tertiary roads, rated by terrain, the 2026 mudflow and rivers, with whether the radar could watch each stretch from the version 2 flags. 28.2 of 153.4 km could not be watched from Track 48; counting Track 98 as well, 4.8 km.

capabilities.name: Road-segment evidence inspector: why a stretch is rated as it is, what the radar saw there, from which file, and what to verify
capabilities.evidence: Every stretch has a stable ID from its OSM way. The panel and every report format are built from one record; a test checks they carry the same values.

capabilities.name: Field-check list: records made from real road stretches, statuses, human field reports and exports
capabilities.evidence: Records start from a shipped road stretch and keep a frozen copy of its satellite evidence. Verified and Not confirmed need a field report with a finding, a date and a source; a report never edits the satellite copy. Saved in one browser only, with JSON import and JSON, CSV, GeoJSON and printable exports. No real field report has been received: the project has none.
tests: frontend/e2e/real.spec.ts::a road stretch becomes a field-check record

capabilities.name: What to try next: rule-based next steps for spots the radar cannot use
capabilities.evidence: A fixed rule table turns each observability reason into a next step and says whether the evidence is already in CascadeLens, only catalogued, not found, or needs a person. It never claims an acquisition exists that the manifest does not hold.
tests: frontend/e2e/real.spec.ts::a spot the radar cannot use gets rule-based next steps

capabilities.name: Road access to health care (screen): which places keep a road path when reported damage is closed, and which closures cause each change
capabilities.evidence: OSM roads (HOT export) with destroyed status and the HOT bridge damage assessment. 20 of 26 named places have a road path to a health facility with every road open, 10 with reported damage closed. The network stops at the study area, so detours beyond it are not found.

capabilities.name: Readiness engine: how far each flood and landslide capability could honestly go, from the data on disk
capabilities.evidence: Twelve capabilities (F0 to F5, L0 to L5) checked against eleven conditions per dataset, and against their model, calibration and validation records. Today two are context only, two have data but need processing (L2: the BIPAD inventory states no licence; L4: the NISAR series ends a week before its window closes), and eight are not available; each names its next requirement. A validation that missed its own criterion is listed but does not count.

capabilities.name: Rainfall-triggered landslide thresholds (Model B, L2)
capabilities.evidence: Run on real data on 13 November 2026: IMERG Late daily rainfall and BIPAD landslide reports, fitted on 2016-2022, calibrated on 2023-2024, scored on 2025-2026 as the rainfall would have been published. Corridor CSI 0.20 against a chance 95th percentile of 0.21 (p = 0.12): it missed its pre-stated criterion, so no warning is offered. BIPAD states no licence, and the readiness engine holds L2 there until NDRRMA confirms terms (docs/MODELS.md).

capabilities.name: Flood forecasting (GloFAS, river gauges)
capabilities.evidence: No forecast data loaded. The what-if flood is an illustration, labelled as such.

capabilities.name: Rasuwa simulations: flow replay, what-if flood, radar explainer
capabilities.evidence: Illustrations built on real geography, labelled as not forecasts.

capabilities.name: Tsho Rolpa glacial lake case (GCOV lake area, compare, 3D, scenario, coherence)
capabilities.evidence: 4 GCOV dates and a coherence layer, rebuilt from the event pair on 13 Nov. The product's mask marks most of the lake as water, so no lake median is quoted. Dam and glacier movement bounds are research output only and are not shown.

capabilities.name: Automatic download and live processing
capabilities.evidence: NASA Earthdata downloads need a login and are done by hand by design; the app is a static site.

capabilities.name: Machine-learning landslide or flood prediction
capabilities.evidence: No labelled data at the needed scale. The first models are deliberately simple and transparent (thresholds, logistic regression, GR4J), and none is run until its data exists.

capabilities.name: Public hosted version
capabilities.evidence: Waiting on the team's choice of hosting.
